calls.reason: MIT and Boston University researchers tested GPT-4's reasoning with altered task rules without training-data access. Their work challenges the claimed impossibility of serious scrutiny, although it used the released checkpoint.

The March 16 technical report disclosed Transformer architecture, next-token training, broad data sources and RLHF. Important details remained secret, but the assertion of total nondisclosure goes too far.

OpenAI's launch evidence shows persistent reliability problems alongside substantial exam gains. It does not establish whether strengths changed qualitatively, and the claim supplies no clear boundary.

NewsGuard documented misinformation failures, while OpenAI published safety metrics and Bing documented conversation limits. This mixed record establishes neither comprehensive safety nor an absence of usable measures and constraints.
